data.name: Bildad
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word ‘b’l-dalet’ meaning ‘man of God’. This name is mentioned in Job 8:1, and Bildad is one of Job’s three friends who come to console him.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes dedication and devotion to God.
data.numerology_meaning: The 6 Life Path Number indicates that the person born with this name has a deep inner sense of responsibility, and a strong desire to help others.

in_hebrew.name: בילדד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: בילדד בן שואח הוא אחד מחבריו של איוב המוזכרים בספר איוב בתנך. השם בילדד עשוי להיות מורכב משתי מילים: ביל ודד, שיכולים להיות מתורגמים כ ביל- דוד או בן דד. לא ברור אם השם הוא ממקור שמית או שאינו שמית.

in_greek.name: Βιλδὰδ
in_greek.long_meaning: Βιλδὰδ ὁ Σαυχίτης, ἕνας τῶν φίλων τοῦ Ιώβ, ἀναφέρεται εἰς τὸ βιβλίον Ιώβ τῆς Καινῆς Διαθήκης. Ὁ Βιλδὰδ οὐκ ἔχει σαφῆ ἐτυμολογίαν ἀπὸ τῆς ἑβραϊκῆς γλώσσης.

in_latin.name: Bildad
in_latin.long_meaning: Bildad, filius Suh, unus ex amicis Iob, commemoratur in libro Iob Veteris Testamenti. Nomen Bildad non habet certam etymologiam latina.

in_english.name: Bildad
in_english.meaning: Friend of Job, son of Shuah
in_english.long_meaning: Bildad is a biblical name borne by one of Job's friends, mentioned in the Book of Job. The name likely comes from the Hebrew 'Bil'dad', possibly meaning 'son of contention' or 'without contention'. Its etymology is uncertain. Bildad is categorized under biblical names and Christian tradition.

biblical_reference.note: Bildad is one of Job's three friends who come to comfort him.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bildad has historical significance in Western culture, particularly in the realm of literature and theology. In the biblical book of Job, Bildad is recognized as a distinguished man from the land of Adam, and he is considered one of the ancient sages of the Old Testament. Bildad's philosophical insights and moral assessments provide insight and thus contribute greatly to a better understanding of human suffering and God's role in it. In various literary works, the character of Bildad has been used to illustrate the themes of moral support, life struggles, and the importance of community during times of adversity.
data.spiritual_significance: Bildad’s name carries a deep spiritual importance rooted in the ancient Biblical tradition. It underscores the belief that even in the midst of human trials and sufferings, one can still turn to God for solace and guidance. Bildad represents the idea that the man of God, through faith and wisdom, can provide comfort and direction to those who face life's most challenging situations. By bearing this name, one expresses a commitment to the spiritual journey and a desire to live a life steeped in the wisdom and grace of God.

historical_references.reference: Bildad, one of the three friends of Job, is a Shuhite, and a man of great experience and wisdom. He is described as a man 'terrible as a burned out lamp, as a clay jar shattered by the earth, as a man with black eyes set in the darkest night.' (Job 2:11, 13)
historical_references.context: Book of Job, Old Testament, Bible

historical_references.reference: Bildad is presented as a wise elder who speaks to Job from a position of authority and experience. He emphasizes the importance of confession and submission to God, arguing that Job's suffering is a result of his sin. (Job 8:2-7)
historical_references.context: Book of Job, Old Testament, Bible

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Bildad continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Hannah Bildad from Jerusalem, Israel embodies the meaning of Bildad - "Man of God". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Bildad, derived from the Hebrew word "baldad," means "swift or speedy to act." In a spiritual context, it symbolizes one who is quick to respond to God's call and eager to apply divine wisdom in daily life.
